fault_injection_probe.what_was_done: Did NOT run the full fc.assert suite (would consume the S7 12-minute / 720s wall-clock envelope, which this story is explicitly forbidden from spending). Did NOT inject any fault into the committed file — none is present. Instead, verified the structural guarantee that a counterexample naming a C.* command is intrinsic to the DSL.
fault_injection_probe.structural_guarantee: arbActor = fc.constantFrom<ActorId>('A','B','C') feeds every per-actor command (Lg/Ct/Ut/Sc/As/Un/Dt/Rl), and each of those commands' toString() returns `${this.actor}.Verb(args)`. Concretely: C.Ct(title), C.Ut(title), C.Sc(open), C.As(pubkeyA), C.Un(task), C.Dt(task), C.Rl(), C.Lg(group) are all reachable shrink outputs. Therefore any 3-party-only divergence whose minimal reproduction involves C will render at least one `C.*` token in fast-check's verbose counterexample chain. The only A-anchored commands (A.Cg, A.In(B|C), A.Fd, A.Sw(B)) are A-only by the admin/MIP-03 model and never mask a C action. The naming format Actor.Verb(args) (AC-X-NAMING-3P-1) is thus enforced by construction, not by a one-off probe.
fault_injection_probe.s7_followup: S7's manual AC-VAL-3P-1 will perform the live demonstration: comment out C's relay subscription (or break a C-side assertion), run make e2e against the 3P file, observe a counterexample chain that includes a C.* command plus a B-or-A-dispatched task event C cannot see post-quiesce, then revert. That is the empirical confirmation; S5 provides the structural one.

The 3P file does NOT do per-iteration re-authentication (unlike the 2-party file, which re-auths each iteration against its spawnSpecBunker keypairs to shed accumulated pending-invitations). verification.rd_vs_rl_finding: CONFIRMED — the architect's exclusion of RdCommand3P from the commands array is CORRECT. The spec's commands array (spec.md:232) lists the per-actor task commands as a comment placeholder: `// ... CtCommand3P, UtCommand3P, ScCommand3P, AsCommand3P, UnCommand3P, DtCommand3P, RlCommand3P` — it names RlCommand3P (reload, A11 persistence), NOT RdCommand3P (rename device). The S2 port list (spec.md:276) likewise lists 'RlCommand' not 'RdCommand'. Rd appears in the spec only in the broader command-vocabulary line (spec.md:31) and the S3 port list (spec.md:277), which port Rd into the file as a class — but Rd is intentionally NOT wired into the property-run array. AC-3P-RUN-1 requires exactly the listed arbitraries with no additions; since the spec array lists Rl and not Rd, including Rd would VIOLATE AC-3P-RUN-1. The exclusion is correct.
verification.rd_unused_observation: MINOR CLEANLINESS (not a failure): RdCommand3P is defined (lines 918-950, from S3 per AC-3P-RD-1) but deliberately unwired into the commands array — a defined-but-unused class. verification.fd_shape_observation: MINOR SPEC INCONSISTENCY (not a failure): spec.md:231 writes the Fd arbitrary as `arbActor.map(a => new FdCommand3P(a))` (per-actor), which contradicts the normative AC-3P-FD-1 (acceptance-criteria.md:34) defining FdCommand3P as admin-only with an actor-free A-only check. The implementation correctly follows AC-3P-FD-1 (`fc.constant(new FdCommand3P())`, A-only). The command-TYPE set is exact; only the spec-snippet's Fd shape diverges, and the impl resolves the conflict in favor of the AC. Recommend the spec author reconcile spec.md:231 with AC-3P-FD-1 in a future doc edit.
